inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors

instructions.note: The prompt directs MFA reset and temporary pass delivery based on ticket opener identity without requiring independent verification that the requester is the account owner.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced outside the model, but effectiveness degrades operationally at high approval volume through approval fatigue; autonomy increase or removal would defeat it.

controls.name: Bind temporary pass delivery to verified account owner channel
Require independent identity verification before MFA reset
Tamper-evident attributable record linking requester verification, approver, target account, and pass delivery

findings.title: Authority laundering via requester-bound temporary pass after analyst-approved MFA reset (TC9/TC4)

attack_path.note: Contractor or vendor can open a ticket by email; requester field is the email sender.
Agent looks up the target user profile and memberships.
Agent removes MFA methods and issues a temporary pass after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is sent to the ticket opener, not the account owner.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed, or analyst queue volume rises further while the design still routes temporary passes to the requester rather than the verified account owner.

evidence.observation: The prompt says for MFA problems to look up the user, reset MFA, and send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
The analyst sees the exact target account, requester, and full ticket body, so the approval gate is raw action review.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in; the requester field is the email sender; the temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, which makes approval volume high and weakens the gate's residual credit.

recommendations.action: Deliver the temporary pass only to a verified account-owner channel from the identity system of record, not to the ticket requester field.
Require an independent identity verification step before allowing MFA reset for email-originated or contractor-submitted tickets.

findings.title: Missing attributable action record for privileged identity recovery actions

forecast.watch_signal: No trigger changes this rating because the restoring control is absent; reassess when a tamper-evident attributable record is implemented.

evidence.observation: The artifact shows what analysts see for approval but does not describe a tamper-evident attributable record linking requester verification, approver decision, target account, and actual temporary-pass recipient.

The design performs consequential identity actions: MFA reset and sending a temporary pass externally. The provided artifacts do not declare an attributable audit record whose integrity would make those actions non-repudiable.

recommendations.action: Create a tamper-evident, attributable record for each reset that binds requester identity evidence, analyst approver, target user, issued temporary pass event, and delivery destination.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided design does not expose self-configuration, tool mutation, or mutable external definitions for this agent.
The artifacts show bounded steps and no open-ended loop, spend path, or recursive delegation for this design.
This external entity is only the asserted requester source; the main issue here is impersonation, not auditability of the entity itself.
The inbound ticket flow brings data into the agent; the evidenced risk is malicious content and identity assertion, not disclosure on this flow.
No evidence in the artifacts indicates the inbound ticket flow can exhaust resources beyond routine queue load.
The key issue on the outbound pass flow is sending to the wrong recipient, not in-transit integrity failure described by the artifacts.
The artifacts do not indicate this outbound messaging flow can be abused for service exhaustion in the assessed design.
The artifacts describe queue contents and approval volume but do not state integrity protections on the approval queue records.
The artifacts do not say who can read stored queue records or whether ticket bodies in the queue are access-controlled.
The artifacts do not describe queue availability protections, rate limits, or backlog handling for the approval system.

rating.rationale: Present inherent risk is critical because an untrusted ticket requester can influence confidential directory read, irreversible MFA reset, and external delivery of a temporary pass to the requester. The only declared preventive control is a raw-action analyst approval gate on reset, but at about 400 approvals per shift across two analysts it is high-volume and earns only one tier of residual credit, leaving the main path at high. Forecast returns to critical if autonomy increases or the approval gate is removed. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, tool manifest, or IdP/chat integration configuration was provided, so credential scope, delivery mechanics, and audit properties are assessed from prompt and runtime notes only.
No explicit audit-log or identity-verification artifact was provided; the property finding assumes those controls are absent from the declared design rather than disproving their runtime existence.
